question: Does adding only the immediately previous observed physical residual causally improve next-factual-effect prediction versus F8-R2's 28-coefficient fully observed linear7 baseline on the same already-consumed F7 worlds, or is F7 effectively Markov for this limited comparison?

data.source: previously consumed F7 factual 128 x 96 no source replay
data.cohort: 80 FIT, 16 FIT-selector, 32 old FIT-holdout (already used, NOT fresh generalization)
data.x: P80 normalized 7D state/action key for factual events 2..96
data.y: P80 4D tanh normalized physical deltas for exactly the corresponding factual effects

fitting.baseline: same F8-R2 float64 normal equation ridge selection on fit80, select lambda on old16 selector; refit linear7 on first96, no use of last32 during fitting
fitting.memory: augment frozen 28-parameter linear7 predictor with 4x4 signed first-order last-factual-residual correction; no memory at first included event in world; residual from time t-1 strictly after actual chosen action; never y[t] at t
fitting.memory_training: fit delta correction on 80 fit worlds using baseline fit80 residual at t>=1; choose ridge lambda using 16 fit-selector worlds, with their past factual residuals available; refit both baseline linear and memory correction on first96; evaluate only last32 existing old holdout
fitting.objective: mean square error of 4 normalized factual delta channels per world with exactly 95 events
fitting.negative: shift prior residual by +7 across *within-world* history; preserve marginal values but destroy immediately preceding action-residual alignment; negative uses learned correction weights unmodified
fitting.numeric_guard: all finite, shape and source receipt/episode identity locked by existing F8-R2 read_spent

provenance.model_training_type: authorized source-neutral closed-form retrospective linear fit only

qualification.engineering: full original G4 on exact final SHA on Windows/Ubuntu, G5 Windows/Ubuntu, G7 Ubuntu, negative controls
